binding: local CLI; discover operations with vamp commands and types with vamp schema

identity.library: Stable UUID in library.json; contexts are machine-local connection configuration, not libraries.
identity.asset: Stable UUID independent of original path or byte digest.
identity.original: Regular-file bytes with BLAKE3 digest of exact bytes. Original {path, blake3, byte_size, mime, locator?, storage, hash_state, modified_ns?}: path is the authority-local copy ('' once evicted); locator names the verified cloud copy (s3://bucket/key or folder://default/<relpath>); storage is local | uploading | cloud+local | cloud. Catalogs without these fields read as storage local, hash_state hashed.
identity.lazy_fingerprint: References cataloged without reading bytes (Eagle import; Google Drive placeholders) have hash_state pending, blake3 '' and size + modified_ns from stat. Their source key is pending:<byte_size>:<modified_ns> (Original::source_key; blake3 once hashed): every source-keyed record (representations, observations, embeddings, jobs, uploads, assets.hash, replica cache names with ':' -> '-') uses it. The digest is computed whenever the bytes are read anyway: native original (viewer), thumbnail/preview generation, processors with original input, cloud upload, export, media add/refresh of that path, or explicitly via media hash / native hash. If size and mtime still match, every source-keyed record is rekeyed to the digest without a revision bump (event media_hashed); otherwise the original changed since cataloging and it is a refresh (revision bump, derivatives dropped, media_updated change original). Dedupe: add of a pending path resolves it in place. Pending assets are never evicted.
identity.representation: A role and source key associated with an asset; local paths are relative to catalog state.
identity.collection: A folder: nested via parent_id (null = root), ordered among siblings by sort_order; membership ordered by insertion and does not own or copy original bytes. Names need not be unique.
identity.asset_facts: Asset {width?, height?, original_created_at?, original_modified_at?, last_viewed_at?, deleted_at?}; Metadata {rating 0-5, colors [{hex #rrggbb, ratio 0-1}] largest first}. Dimensions come from the source catalog (Eagle) or a generated derivative's source size; colors from Eagle palettes or vamp-media palette on the thumbnail. Derived facts do not advance revision.

storage.authority: One local catalog authority; SQLite serializes mutations on that machine. Not a multi-device sync protocol.
storage.configuration: --home, VAMP_HOME, or $HOME/.local/share/vamp; config.json selects named contexts.
storage.original_root: Optional base for relative paths passed to media add; stored original locators are canonical absolute paths.
storage.local_state: Local catalog, durable jobs, model observations and generated representations. Keep outside cloud-placeholder original storage.
storage.pinning: Generated representations persist until explicitly removed outside VAMP. Rehydrated cloud originals persist in cache/originals until vamp cache prune.
storage.offline: Listing, browse, sidebar, metadata search, inspection, events, metadata export, Eagle import/sync and local-representation fetch never read originals (stat only). Sheet generation only reads existing thumbnails.
explicit_original_reads: native original (viewer; also settles a pending fingerprint)
media thumbnail/preview when not already generated
storage.fetch: Returns an available filesystem path, not bytes. Does not substitute another representation. Cloud-stored originals without a local copy are downloaded, verified, into state_dir/cache/originals (see storage.cloud.fetch).
storage.deletion: media remove / native remove moves to the trash (deleted_at set, memberships kept, restorable with restore). media empty-trash / native empty_trash tombstones catalog metadata and removes memberships. Neither deletes the referenced original. The sole exception anywhere in VAMP is the opt-in storage.cloud.delete_local_after_upload eviction.
storage.export: vamp export: metadata and locators only, including tombstones, asset-linked derivatives, observations, collections and event history. Not a self-contained media archive; executable processor configuration is intentionally excluded. Copying original bytes out is media export / native export.

cloud.purpose: Optional per-library backend holding full-resolution originals; thumbnails/previews always stay in local state. Replicas and apps fetch originals on demand through the authority.
cloud.configure: vamp storage set s3 --bucket B [--prefix P] --endpoint URL [--region R] [--path-style] [--save-credentials] | vamp storage set folder --root DIR (iCloud Drive, Google Drive, Dropbox, NAS...); vamp storage show | unset. Stored in the catalog settings table (key storage). unset is refused while any original is cloud-only; switching backend kind is refused while locators of the other kind exist.
cloud.credentials: S3 only: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from the environment, else <state_dir>/storage-credentials.json (mode 0600, written by --save-credentials). Never in the catalog, events, exports or StoreRequest.
cloud.keys: <prefix><library_id>/originals/<blake3[0:2]>/<blake3><.ext> (folder: under --root without prefix). Content-addressed, so re-uploads are idempotent. VAMP never deletes cloud objects.
cloud.upload_queue: media add/ingest and a changed-original refresh (while a backend is configured) set storage uploading and insert a durable uploads row (asset_id, source_hash) in the same transaction. vamp storage migrate [--limit] queues existing local originals and re-queues failed ones. Uploads drain in jobs run / jobs watch and the vamp-server background worker under the library worker lock; rows left running by a crash are redone (idempotent). vamp storage uploads [--status] lists them; statuses pending|running|completed|failed|skipped.
cloud.verify: Upload re-hashes the local file first (refuses changed bytes; run media refresh). Folder: copy to a same-directory temp, fsync, rename, fsync dir, then re-read and compare blake3+size. S3: vamp-store hashes exactly the bytes sent (fails before completing on mismatch), stores x-amz-meta-blake3, then HEAD must match size and blake3. Only then locator is set, storage becomes cloud+local and event original_stored is emitted.
cloud.delete_local_after_upload: DANGER, default OFF. --delete-local-after-upload is the ONLY path in which VAMP deletes an original. When on, after a verified upload and once a thumbnail AND preview exist for the current hash, the local file is deleted only if its size and blake3 still match the cloud copy, and only if it lies under original_root or the inbox unless --delete-local-anywhere is also set. The asset becomes storage cloud with path '' and event original_evicted {previous_path, locator} is emitted. Modified files are never deleted; they stay cloud+local until refreshed.
cloud.fetch: fetch original / native original+representation / GET /v1/assets/{id}/original: the local copy when present, else <state_dir>/cache/originals/<blake3><.ext> (pinned until vamp cache prune), else download from the backend into that cache via temp file with blake3 verification. A corrupt or missing cloud copy is an error, never served. Concurrent downloads of one hash are serialized by a per-hash file lock (cache/originals/.<blake3>.lock); waiters reuse the verified result. vamp-server resolves the locator under the library lock and downloads after releasing it, so other requests are not blocked.
cloud.refresh: refresh on a cloud-only original fails with a clear error (no local file to compare); fetch it and add an edited file as a new asset.
cloud.helper: S3 goes through the separate vamp-store executable (VAMP_STORE_HELPER, beside the running executable, or app Resources): one StoreRequest JSON {operation put|get|head|delete|presign, endpoint, region, bucket, key, path_style, path?, blake3?, content_type?, expires_seconds?} on stdin, one StoreResponse {exists, byte_size?, blake3?, url?} on stdout, ErrorResponse on stderr with exit 1. SigV4 via rusty-s3 + ureq; multipart in 16 MiB parts above 64 MiB. Core has no S3 dependencies.

mutations.revision: Asset revision advances on metadata updates, changed-original refresh, trash/restore and tombstoning. Derived representations and observations, derived facts (dimensions, palette), touch (last_viewed_at) and lazy-hash resolution do not advance asset revision.
mutations.precondition: --expected-revision rejects a stale mutation without changing metadata or emitting an event. Without it, the transaction applies to current catalog state.
mutations.add: Repeated add of the same canonical live path and digest returns the existing asset. Changed bytes require explicit refresh. A tombstoned path is not silently resurrected. Equal bytes at different paths can remain distinct assets.
mutations.refresh: Rehashes original explicitly. Changed bytes retain asset identity, advance revision, invalidate derivative associations and exclude old-source observations from inspection/search.
mutations.missing_original: Unavailability does not remove metadata, invalidate cached representations or imply deletion.
mutations.metadata_patch: Omitted/null fields are unchanged. Empty strings clear textual content; an empty tag array clears tags. add_tags/remove_tags apply after tags. rating 0-5. Tags are trimmed, sorted and deduplicated.
mutations.search: SQLite FTS5 token search across names, descriptions, tags, source URLs and current-source observation JSON. Quoted tokens are combined with AND. Not vector/semantic search. Trashed assets are excluded unless browsing with trash:true.

events.collections: collection_updated payload is {collection_id,asset_id,operation:add|remove} for membership, {collection_id,name,operation:rename}, {collection_id,parent_id,index,operation:move} or {collection_id,name,operation:eagle_sync}. collection_deleted payload {collection_id,name}; deletion removes memberships only, never assets; child folders move up to the deleted folder's parent.
events.organization: smart_folder_updated {smart_folder_id?, operation create|update|delete|eagle_sync} and tag_groups_updated {} carry no asset; replicas refetch smart folders / tag groups (POST /v1/native smart_folders, tags). media_trashed {original_deleted:false, reason?}, media_restored {}, media_viewed {} and media_hashed {blake3, previous_key} carry the asset.
events.ordering: Monotonic sequence within one library; events --after uses an exclusive cursor. UUID event identities are independent of sequence.
events.atomicity: Catalog mutation, its event, and configured pending jobs commit in the same transaction.
events.actor: VAMP_ACTOR or local; attribution only, not authentication or authorization.
events.replay: Consumers retain their last sequence and request later events. Events are retained; no retention truncation is implemented.
events.storage: original_upload_queued {blake3} (storage migrate); original_stored {locator, blake3, byte_size}; original_evicted {previous_path, locator}. Each advances asset revision; replicas re-fetch the AssetView and receive storage state.

processors.trust: Explicitly registered local executables; argv passed directly, never through a shell. They run with the user's permissions and are not sandboxed. Imported/shared media cannot register code.
processors.representation_ready: Only enqueues processors whose configured input role equals the ready representation role.
processors.request: One ToolRequest JSON document on stdin; original/thumbnail/preview input selected explicitly. A missing thumbnail/preview input is generated from the original first when the vamp-media helper is available (local jobs and the authority's representation endpoint, so remote workers get it too); otherwise, and for originals, a missing input fails without fallback.
processors.response: One ToolResponse JSON document on stdout; diagnostics on stderr. Processors return observations or generated representations; they do not edit the catalog directly.
processors.limits: 1 MiB request, 4 MiB response, 64 KiB captured stderr, timeout 1–3600 seconds. Unix process groups are terminated when the finite job exits or times out.
processors.execution: Ingestion enqueues durably. jobs run drains a bounded batch; jobs watch continuously drains. No scheduler, installed service or GUI is required.
processors.dedupe: At most one pending/running job per (asset, processor, current original source hash): triggers and vamp processors enqueue return the existing job instead of queueing another (no processing_requested event); jobs retry refuses while one is active.
processors.bulk: vamp processors enqueue-all NAME [--missing-only] queues NAME for every live asset, skipping assets with an active job and, with --missing-only, those whose current original already has a completed job of NAME -> {processor, enqueued, already_queued, already_completed}. vamp jobs cancel [--status pending|failed (default pending)] [--processor NAME] deletes matching jobs (never running ones) -> {cancelled}.
processors.configuration_snapshot: Queued jobs retain registration configuration even if that processor is later edited or removed.
processors.crash_recovery: A subsequent exclusive local worker marks abandoned running jobs failed, except jobs holding a remote lease. Retrying is explicit; subprocess side effects may have already happened. Leased jobs whose lease expired return to pending (error notes the expiry) on the next claim or local run, or fail after 3 attempts.
processors.placement: ProcessorSpec.placement any (default, omitted) | local | remote, read from the CURRENT registration (vamp processors placement NAME any|local|remote). The authority's local worker (run_jobs, vamp-server's drain) skips remote; /v1/jobs/claim skips local. remote requires output observation. Job claims are compare-and-set on status, so a local worker and remote workers never run the same job.
processors.staleness: Input-source digest must match current asset both before processing and before applying results. Stale jobs cannot annotate replacement bytes.
processors.idempotency: An observation's ID is its job ID, preventing duplicate application after retry. Existing current-source derivative roles are reused. External subprocess side effects are not exactly-once.
processors.feedback: Observation events cannot trigger processors; already-present current-source derivatives avoid representation cycles.
processors.privacy: Bundled Florence processor runs offline against local previews. Arbitrary user-supplied processors may access the network; thumbnails remain sensitive media.

optional_capabilities.core: No image decoder, Python, ML runtime or model weights in core dependency graph. setup without --install is read-only file-presence inspection.
optional_capabilities.media: Separate vamp-media executable, installed explicitly from a locked source checkout. JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/TIFF/BMP; first frame/page only; decoder-supported orientation; no ICC color conversion. On macOS, formats the image crate cannot decode (HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, PSD, ...) fall back to the system sips converter bounded to 4096px. Video preview generation is not included.
optional_capabilities.florence: Explicit uv environment and pinned native Transformers-compatible Florence-2-base model installation. No remotely supplied Python model code. Caption observations become searchable text; vector search is the separate models capability.
optional_capabilities.models: vamp setup models --install [--device auto|cpu|cuda|mps]: one uv env (processors/pyproject.toml pins) at <home>/tools/models with Florence-2-base (description + tags) and SigLIP base patch16-224 (embeddings), pinned revisions, and registers processors florence-description, florence-tags, siglip-embedding plus the text embedder in the active/--context library. --device defaults to cuda on Linux when `nvidia-smi -L` succeeds (torch installed with uv --torch-backend cu128), else cpu; the chosen device is recorded in <home>/tools/models/device and used by later inspection and vamp worker. The text embedder always uses --device auto (cuda, then mps, then cpu). See models section.
optional_capabilities.contact_sheets: JPEG output with numbered tiles and an explicit number/asset-ID/coordinate map. Existing outputs are never overwritten. No guaranteed vision-token savings.
optional_capabilities.browser_clipper: clients/browser-extension (MV3, Chromium + Firefox 121+, unpacked, no build). Talks only to vamp-server with a bearer token from options (chrome.storage.local). Image: POST /v1/clip {url,title,image_url,tags,note?}. Bookmark: POST /v1/clip {url,title,tags,note?}. Visible-tab screenshot: POST /v1/ingest raw image/png with ?filename=<title>.png&name=&source_url=&tags=a,b&note=. Connection test: GET /v1/library. Accepts bare JSON or {ok,data,error} envelopes.

models.tags_observation: kind "tags", value {"tags":[string]} (Florence <OD> labels then <CAPTION> words; lowercase, dedup, stopwords and -ing words removed, max 12). Indexed for full-text search like any observation.
models.suggested_tags: inspect AssetView.suggested_tags: lowercase tags from current-original tags observations minus the user's tags (case-insensitive). Never merged into metadata.tags automatically.
models.accept_tags: CLI vamp media accept-tags <id> [TAG..] [--expected-revision N]; native accept_tags{asset_id,tags}. Each tag must be a current suggestion; empty list accepts all; none available is an error. Normal metadata update (revision bump, media_updated event). Returns Asset.
models.embedding_observation: kind "embedding", value {"embedding":{model,dim(1..8192),vector_b64: dim f32 little-endian}}. Core L2-normalizes and stores the vector in table embeddings(asset_id,source_hash,model,dim,vector BLOB) keyed by the job's source digest; vector_b64 is stripped from the stored observation so it never enters the search index. Malformed vectors fail the job and store nothing.
models.embedder: Per-library text embedder {command:[...], model, timeout_seconds?=120, serve?=false} (vamp embedder set --spec FILE | show | remove). Requests are ToolRequest {operation:"embed_text", text}; the answer must be an embedding observation whose model equals the configured model. serve=false: one-shot subprocess per query. serve=true: core sends one JSON line per connection to the Unix socket <state_dir>/embedder.sock (or $TMPDIR/vamp-embedder-<blake3(state_dir)[..16]>.sock when that path is >=100 bytes) and reads one ToolResponse line ({"error":...} on failure). If nothing is listening, core starts `command --serve --socket PATH --idle-seconds 900` detached (own process group, stderr appended to <state_dir>/embedder.log) and answers that query one-shot. Any server failure also falls back to one-shot. The server binds the socket 0600 before loading the model, refuses to start if another server answers on it, replaces a stale socket, and removes it on idle exit or SIGTERM.
models.semantic_search: vamp media search --semantic TEXT [--limit N] [--hybrid] -> {semantic:true,hybrid,elapsed_ms,results:[{asset,score}]}. Brute-force cosine over current-revision, non-deleted embeddings of the embedder model; stale (pre-refresh) vectors never match. --hybrid ranks by reciprocal rank fusion (k=60) of semantic and FTS ranks; score is then the fused value.
models.similar: vamp media similar <id> [--limit N]; native similar{asset_id,limit?=40} -> {items:[browse_item+score]}. Uses the asset's current-original embedding (embedder model preferred), excludes the asset itself; errors if it has none.
models.energy_pack: native energy_pack{} -> {path, version, model, dim, palette_dim, count, quant:"int8", bytes} or {count:0} without embeddings. Local file for in-memory similarity browsing (Mac Same Energy mode). Authority: built from live, untrashed assets' current-original embeddings of the embedder model (else the most common model) and cached at <state_dir>/energy/pack.bin, rebuilt when the fingerprint of (asset id, source hash, colors) rows changes. Replica: mirrored from GET /v1/embeddings/pack after syncs that applied changes (or when missing); answered from the mirror while a background check fetches a newer version. Format (little endian): b"VEPK0001", u32 header length, header JSON {format:1, version, model, dim, palette_dim:64, count, quant, ids}, zero pad to 16 bytes, f32 scales[count], i8 vibe[count*dim] (vector = scale*q, per-row symmetric), u8 palette[count*64] (value/255 of an L2-normalized 4x4x4 Gaussian CIELAB histogram weighted by swatch ratio; all zero without colors).
models.native_browse: browse{semantic:true, query} ranks by embedding cosine. Every browse filter (folders, smart folder, tags, exts, shape, rating, colors, dates, trash, ...) picks the candidates before ranking; total counts all ranked candidates, and offset/limit page through them. sort is ignored. Items are browse_items plus score, and the response includes semantic:true. With no configured embedder, or an empty query, it runs the ordinary browse with all filters and adds semantic:false.
models.latency: Apple Silicon, 960px previews, CPU float32 one-shot processors: florence-description ~4.4 s/image, florence-tags ~4.0 s/image, siglip-embedding ~1.6 s/image (Python import + weight load dominate; MPS was not faster one-shot, Florence tags 10.5 s on MPS vs 4.7 s CPU, so processors stay on --device cpu). Remote vamp worker on an RTX 4090 (--device cuda, float32, warm servers; 10 real images, process_ms excluding ~15 ms download over the tailnet): florence-description median 1.2 s (0.65-1.7 s), florence-tags 0.45 s, siglip-embedding 31 ms; the first job per processor pays ~4-7 s server start; one-shot CUDA runs were slower than the Mac CPU (7.9/7.0/5.1 s) because of CUDA init + load, hence warm servers. Semantic queries with the default persistent embedder (--device auto -> MPS): first query ~2.2 s (one-shot while the server starts), warm queries ~10 ms end-to-end through the CLI (CPU server ~23 ms). Brute-force cosine is negligible at catalog scale. Image embeddings computed on CUDA and the Mac's text/image embeddings use the same pinned SigLIP revision (cosine 1.0 between Mac CPU and 4090 CUDA vectors of the same preview), so mixed-device catalogs rank consistently. Models on disk: Florence-2-base 454 MB, SigLIP base 778 MB; uv env ~565 MB.

native.remote_attach: {name, remote_url, token?} -> {name, library_id, state_dir, remote_url, sync}. Verifies the token against GET /v1/library, creates a replica mirror (state_dir under <home>/replicas/), registers the context with remote {url, token}, then runs sync (snapshot bootstrap) and returns once catalog metadata is mirrored; thumbnails download in the background. Re-attaching the same name to the same authority resumes (an interrupted attach); another authority under that name is refused. Requires vamp-core feature `remote` (enabled in vamp-bridge). token absent/empty = Tailscale identity auth; remote_url may be host[:port] (normalized like `vamp join`).
native.sync: {context?} -> {applied, cursor, snapshot, pending_thumbnails}. Replica contexts only. Cursor 0 (with events) or more than 5000 events behind (GET /v1/hello cursor, checked when an events page is full): bootstrap from GET /v1/snapshot in one transaction (assets absent from it are tombstoned, FTS rebuilt once; applied = live asset count), then replay events after its cursor. Each page of up to 1000 events fetches every changed asset once via POST /v1/assets/batch (absent = tombstone; per-id GET fallback for older authorities) and, on any collection* event, the full collection list. Thumbnails are only queued (eagle_thumbnails kind=download), never downloaded inline: a background downloader in the calling process (app bridge; `vamp sync` drains it before exiting) fetches 8 at a time, prioritize_thumbnails order then newest first, resumable; landed ones appear in thumbnail_updates and the queue in sidebar/sync_status pending_thumbnails. Also: sync_status {context?} -> {syncing, phase? snapshot|applying|events, done?, total?, downloading, pending_thumbnails} (progress of a sync in this process); remote_detach {context} -> {removed} (forgets a replica context and deletes its mirror; local libraries refused).
native.sync_wait: {context?, wait? (s, default 25, max 60)} -> {applied, cursor, changed}. Replica only: long-polls GET /v1/events/stream after the stored cursor and syncs when it returns events.
native.representation: {asset_id, kind: thumbnail|preview|original} -> {path}. Local contexts: the stored file. Replicas: served from state_dir/cache/, downloading on first request (originals verified against blake3). `original` on a replica behaves the same.
native.binding: vamp_request(JSON) C ABI in vamp-bridge; envelope {ok,data,error{code,message}}. Requests up to 96 MiB (base64 ingest). Fields are snake_case; unknown fields are rejected.
native.init: {name, path?} -> context item; creates a library (path = original_root) and makes it current.
native.browse: {query?, semantic?, collection_id?, include_subfolders?, folder_ids?, uncategorized?, smart_folder_id?, kind?, tags?, tags_any?, untagged?, exts?, shape?, rating_min?, colors?, color_tolerance?, date_from?, date_to?, date_field?, size_min?, size_max?, trash?, recently_used?, sort?, seed?, offset, limit 1-500 (default 120)} -> {items,total,offset,has_more}. Every filter composes (AND), also with semantic. collection_id "__uncategorized__" (or uncategorized:true) selects assets in no folder; include_subfolders widens collection_id and folder_ids to their descendants; folder_ids matches any listed folder; smart_folder_id applies that smart folder's rules; kind matches the MIME top-level type; tags are ANDed exact matches, tags_any ORed; untagged selects assets without tags; exts matches the lowercase original extension (any of, leading dot optional); shape (needs asset width/height): square |w-h| <= 5% of the larger, panorama w >= 2h or h >= 2w, landscape w > 1.05h and w < 2h, portrait h > 1.05w and h < 2w; rating_min 1-5; colors ["#rrggbb"] keeps items whose palette distance <= color_tolerance (default 25) where distance = mean over query colors of min over swatches of (CIELAB ΔE76 + 20·(1 − ratio)), so a dominant exact match is ~0 and a small speck ~20; with colors and no sort (or sort color) the order is closest first, and items carry color_distance. date_from/date_to (YYYY-MM-DD, day-inclusive, or RFC 3339) on date_field created (original_created_at else created_at; default) | imported (created_at) | modified (original_modified_at else updated_at). size_min/size_max bound the original byte size (inclusive; the stat size for lazy fingerprints). trash:true lists only trashed assets; otherwise trashed assets are excluded. recently_used:true keeps assets with last_viewed_at. sort: added_desc|added_asc|name_asc|name_desc (case-insensitive)|rating_desc|size_desc|dimensions_desc (width*height)|modified_desc|created_desc|last_viewed_desc (never-viewed last)|random (stable permutation per integer seed, default 0)|color; default: color distance with colors, relevance for queries, else insertion order. Unknown sort is an error. Measured at 20k assets (Apple Silicon, release): page of 200 in 5-20 ms for every filter/sort, sidebar ~37 ms.
native.browse_item: {id,revision,name,ext,mime,byte_size,created_at,original_created_at?,modified (original_modified_at else updated_at),last_viewed_at?,deleted_at?,width?,height? (asset dimensions, else current preview/thumbnail),rating,colors:[{hex,ratio}],tags,description,source_url?,hash_state:hashed|pending,thumbnail_path?,grid_path? (400 px JPEG of the current thumbnail; authority only),preview_path?,available_locally:{thumbnail,preview,original},storage,color_distance? (color browse only)}; original is true when the local copy exists or the original was rehydrated into the cache (replicas: their download cache); storage is Original.storage. Never reads originals: available_locally.original only stats the local path (no hydration) and the rehydration cache.
native.layout: {same filters/sort as browse; micro?: bool} -> {ids, widths, heights (0 = unknown), total, micro? ([base64 JPEG|null])}. Every asset browse would list, in the same order (no paging): clients lay out the whole result at once and fetch cells with `items`. ~10 ms / 110 KB for 2.3k assets; ~40 ms for 22k.
native.items: {asset_ids (max 2000)} -> {items:[browse_item]} in request order; unknown/deleted ids skipped.
native.micro: {asset_ids} -> {micro:{id: base64 JPEG}}. Micro-thumbnails (~40 px, ~1 KB) for every asset with a decodable thumbnail, rendered on the authority by the server's jobs thread (or `generate_thumbs`) together with a 400 px grid JPEG. Replicas pull them in bulk after each sync and fetch missing ones on demand.
native.galaxy: {rebuild?: bool} -> {model, refresh:{model,count,full,added,removed,ms}, ids, xyz (base64 f32 LE, 3 per id, unit-RMS), names, tags (user + suggested, comma-joined), captions (description observation), tints (0xRRGGBB, most vivid palette colour)}. Authority: a 3-D UMAP-style projection of current-original image embeddings (cosine kNN k=15, fuzzy weights, 300 SGD epochs, PCA init; ~0.7 s for 2.3k) stored in table galaxy; new embeddings are placed at the weighted mean of their 8 nearest laid-out neighbours, and a full recompute runs when there is no layout, the model changed, rebuild is set, or incremental placements exceed 20%. Replicas forward to the authority and cache the answer in <state_dir>/galaxy.json, served with offline:<reason> when the authority is unreachable. CLI: vamp galaxy layout [--rebuild] (nightly).
native.galaxy_search: {query, limit?=300 (1..5000)} -> {semantic, ids, scores, embed_ms, ms}. Text-embedder cosine ranking over an in-process copy of the embedding matrix (reloaded when embeddings or liveness change). Replicas forward to the authority (the SigLIP text tower stays there); unreachable -> {semantic:false, ids:[], scores:[], offline}. CLI: vamp galaxy search TEXT [--limit N].
native.generate_thumbs: {} -> {rendered}. Authority only: renders every missing micro/grid thumbnail now (keyed by the thumbnail's source_hash).
native.add: {paths, metadata?: Metadata} -> {assets,errors:[{path,message}]}. Directories expand recursively in sorted order, skipping dot-files. Image assets then get thumbnail+preview from the media helper, plus width/height (source dimensions) and a palette (vamp-media palette op on the thumbnail) recorded without a revision bump; a missing helper or derivative failure leaves the asset without them and is not an error.
native.ingest: {bytes_base64, filename, metadata?} -> Asset. Up to 64 MiB written to the library inbox and referenced; derivatives as for add.
native.update: {asset_id | asset_ids, name?, metadata?: MetadataPatch {name?, description?, tags?, add_tags?, remove_tags?, source_url?, rating? 0-5}, expected_revision? (single asset only)} -> Asset (single) | {assets} (asset_ids). name overrides metadata.name; empty names rejected. tags replaces, then add_tags adds, then remove_tags removes.
native.remove: {asset_ids} -> {trashed}. Moves to the trash (sets deleted_at, keeps folder memberships, advances revision, event media_trashed). Restorable. Originals are never touched.
native.empty_trash: {asset_ids?} -> {deleted}. Tombstones trashed assets (all, or the listed trashed ones): the pre-trash `media remove` semantics — metadata kept as tombstone, memberships removed, event media_removed, originals never deleted.
native.touch: {asset_id} -> {asset_id,last_viewed_at}. Records a view for Recently Used; does not advance revision (event media_viewed).
native.collections_ops: collection_create {name, parent_id?} -> Collection (appended last among siblings); collection_rename {collection_id,name} -> Collection; collection_delete {collection_id} -> {deleted} (children move to the deleted folder's parent); collection_add/collection_remove {collection_id,asset_ids} -> Collection; collection_move {collection_id, parent_id? (null = root), index? (0-based among new siblings, default last)} -> Collection, rejecting cycles; siblings renumbered 0..n.
native.collections: {} -> [{id,name,count,parent_id?,sort_order,color?,icon?,description?,source_id?}] flat, ordered by parent then sort_order; count = live non-trashed direct members.
native.smart_folders: smart_folders {} -> [SmartFolder + count]; smart_folder_create {name, rules:{match:all|any, rules:[{field,op,value}]}, parent_id?} -> SmartFolder; smart_folder_update {smart_folder_id, name?, rules?} -> SmartFolder; smart_folder_delete {smart_folder_id} -> {deleted}. Fields/ops: tags contains|not_contains|any|all|none (value string|[string]; none = untagged) | name, description, url: contains|not_contains|is|is_not|starts_with|ends_with|empty|not_empty | ext: is|is_not|in (case-insensitive) | rating, width, height, size: eq|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte|between ([a,b]) | created, modified, imported: after|before|between|within_days (number) | color: similar (value #rrggbb, optional tolerance on the rule as value [hex, tolerance]) | shape: is|is_not | folder: in|not_in (folder ids, descendants included)|none (uncategorized). Unknown fields/ops are rejected on create/update; untranslatable Eagle rules are kept in `unsupported` and ignored.
native.sidebar: {} -> {pending_thumbnails (Eagle thumbnails queued for import phase B), all, uncategorized, untagged, recently_used, trash, tags_total (distinct tags on live assets), folders:[{id,name,count,parent_id?,sort_order,color?,icon?,children:[...]}] tree (count = direct non-trashed members), smart_folders:[{id,name,count,parent_id?}]}. All counts exclude trashed assets except trash.
native.tags: {} -> {tags:[{tag,count}] over live non-trashed assets (most used first, then by tag), groups:[TagGroup], starred:[tag]}.
native.tag_ops: tag_rename {from, to} -> {updated} renames (merging into an existing `to`) on every live asset and in tag groups; tag_delete {tag} -> {updated} removes it everywhere. Each changed asset advances revision with event media_updated.
native.export: {asset_ids, path} -> {exported:[path], errors:[{asset_id,message}]}. Copies originals (hydrating cloud placeholders; cloud-only originals are fetched first) into the existing directory `path` as <name>.<ext>, suffixing ` (n)` on collisions; never overwrites.
native.import_eagle: {path, hash?: lazy|none|full} -> {library, items, created, updated, unchanged, trashed, restored, skipped:[{item,error}], folders:{created,updated,removed}, smart_folders, tag_groups, queued_thumbnails (copies), queued_generate, missing_thumbnails (items without an Eagle thumbnail), pending_thumbnails (phase B queue size), read_originals (0 unless hash full), hashed}. Synchronous phase A only (thumbnails stay queued). See eagle_import.
native.copy_thumbnails: {limit?} -> {copied, generated, failed, remaining, busy?}. Runs Eagle import phase B synchronously (default: until the queue is empty). busy=true when another copier holds the lock.
native.prioritize_thumbnails: {asset_ids} -> {queued (ids with a queued thumbnail), pending}. Moves them ahead of the phase B queue (latest call first). From the app bridge it also starts a background copier if none runs in-process. Grid calls it (debounced) for visible items lacking thumbnails.
native.thumbnail_updates: {since?} -> {cursor, asset_ids, pending}. Assets whose thumbnail became ready after event cursor since (representation_ready kind thumbnail, at most 1000 events per call, queue order); without since returns only the current cursor. pending = queued Eagle thumbnails.
native.import_eagle_start: {path, hash?} -> {job_id}. Runs the same import on a background thread of the calling process (the app's long-lived bridge); not available over HTTP or on replicas. Path errors surface in import_status.
native.import_status: {job_id} -> {job_id, phase: queued|scanning|folders|items|trash|hashing|done, done, total (units of the current phase: Eagle items, missing items trashed, originals hashed), created, updated, trashed, finished, error?, result? (the import_eagle result once finished without error), thumbnails:{done, total, copied, generated, failed, finished} (phase B, which continues on the same thread after finished=true)}. Progress updates after every batch of up to 500 items or 1 s (100 originals while hashing). Unknown job_id is an error; jobs are kept in memory until the process exits.
native.hash: {limit? (default 100, 1-10000)} -> {hashed, changed, failed:[{asset_id,message}], remaining}. Computes pending fingerprints (reads/hydrates originals). See identity.lazy_fingerprint.
native.palette: {asset_id} -> Asset. Recomputes metadata.colors from the current thumbnail via the media helper (vamp-media operation palette -> ToolResponse.palette); no revision bump, event media_updated {change:palette}.
native.inspect: {asset_id} -> {asset: browse_item, original_path?, source_url, human_description, observations, suggested_tags, representations, created_at, folder_ids, hash_state, blake3?}.
native.find_duplicates: {paths?, bytes_base64?, filename?, hashes?} -> {results:[DuplicateCandidate {path?, filename?, blake3?, byte_size?, error?, matches:[DuplicateMatch {asset_id, basis, trashed, same_path, folder_ids} + item: browse_item]}]}. Intake duplicate screening (the Mac app's Duplicate File Alert). One result per input, in order: each path (directories expand like add) hashed with BLAKE3, then bytes_base64 (with filename for the fallback; at most 64 MiB), then each precomputed hex digest in hashes. Matches are non-tombstoned assets with basis blake3 when the original digest equals the candidate's; trashed assets are included with trashed:true. Assets whose fingerprint is still pending (no digest; see identity.lazy_fingerprint) cannot match by digest: they match only on equal byte_size AND an equal file name (case-insensitive: the asset name, the asset name against the candidate's name without extension, or the original's file name), basis name_size; bytes without filename and digest inputs never fallback-match. Order: live before trashed, then oldest first; at most 20 matches per input. same_path: the candidate path is the asset's original path (add would return that asset instead of a new one). Answered from the local catalog in every context, replicas included (their mirrored asset documents carry the authority's blake3), so no authority round trip happens; reading the candidate files is the only I/O and library originals are never read. Unreadable paths get error and no matches.
native.eagle_import: Eagle library (X.library: images/<ID>.info/{metadata.json, <name>.<ext>, <name>_thumbnail.png}, metadata.json folders/smartFolders/tagsGroups, tags.json). Never opens an original: originals are stat()ed only (pending fingerprint), Two phases. Phase A (import_eagle / import_eagle_start: what the user waits for) writes catalog rows, folders, tags, tag groups and smart folders and queues each item's thumbnail in the durable eagle_thumbnails table (asset_id, kind copy|generate, path, revision, order_key=modificationTime, priority, attempts): copy = Eagle's <name>_thumbnail.png (format sniffed by magic: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP — Eagle often writes WebP into the .png name; stored with the matching extension/mime), generate = image items without one (Eagle shows small originals directly); items are browsable immediately without a thumbnail. Phase B copies queued thumbnails into state_dir/representations/eagle as the thumbnail (source key = current source key; skipped if the asset revision changed since queueing), prioritized ones first (prioritize_thumbnails), then copies before generations, then newest first; generate rows hydrate the original on the worker pool, then render it with the vamp-media helper (Library::generate; settles the lazy fingerprint), in transactions of 48; an interrupted run resumes from the table; a thumbnail failing 3 times is left queued but no longer attempted. Phase B runs in jobs run / jobs watch / the vamp-server worker (run_jobs result thumbnails {copied, generated, failed, remaining}, copied counted in completed), on the app bridge's import thread after phase A, and on a bridge thread started by prioritize_thumbnails when work is queued; one copier per library (state_dir/eagle-thumbnails.lock). Drive reads (metadata.json, .info listing, original stat, thumbnail) run on 24 worker threads; SQLite writes stay single-writer batched transactions.  Mapping: id -> metadata.source_id eagle:<id> (sync key), name -> name (Eagle names exclude the extension; browse items carry ext), tags, annotation -> description, url -> source_url, star -> rating, palettes [{color:[r,g,b], ratio %}] -> colors (ratio/100), width/height, modificationTime -> created_at (Date Imported), btime -> original_created_at, mtime -> original_modified_at, folders -> memberships of folders imported with source_id eagle:<folder id> (nested via children, sibling order kept; description, iconColor -> color, icon), smartFolders -> smart folders (source_id eagle:<id>; first condition's match AND/OR -> all/any; further conditions with another match, negated conditions and unknown properties/methods are kept in unsupported and ignored), tagsGroups -> tag groups (id eagle:<id>), tags.json starredTags -> starred. metadata.extra.eagle = {id, library, stamp, deleted, mt}. Re-running is an incremental sync keyed by Eagle id: items whose root mtime.json entry (id -> lastModified) equals the mt stored at their last import are skipped without opening anything; otherwise items whose modificationTime/lastModified/mtime/isDeleted stamp is unchanged are skipped; changed items replace Eagle-owned fields (revision+1, media_updated change eagle_sync) and re-queue the thumbnail; a changed original path/size/mtime gets a new pending fingerprint; isDeleted items (and items whose .info folder disappeared) move to the trash; items un-deleted in Eagle are restored; Eagle folders/smart folders absent from Eagle are deleted (memberships removed, assets untouched); folders and smart folders made in VAMP are left alone, as are memberships in them. Measured at 20k items (release, local SSD): first import ~23 s, unchanged re-sync ~1.5 s.
native.media_helper: VAMP_MEDIA_HELPER if set, else vamp-media beside the running executable, else ../Resources/vamp-media (macOS app bundle). Operations: generate (thumbnail/preview; RepresentationOutput.source_width/source_height = decoded source size), sheet, palette (input_path -> ToolResponse.palette: up to 8 {hex, ratio} by 4-bit/channel bucketing of a <=64px downscale, near colors merged, largest first).
native.cli: vamp import eagle PATH [--sync] [--hash lazy|none|full] (progress lines `eagle import: <phase> <done>/<total> (created, updated, trashed)` on stderr; the result JSON on stdout); vamp sidebar; vamp media remove|restore|empty-trash|hash [--limit]|export IDS --to DIR; vamp collections create NAME [--parent ID] | move ID [--parent ID] [--index N]; vamp smart list|create NAME RULES_JSON [--parent ID]|update ID [--name] [--rules]|delete ID; vamp tags list|rename FROM TO|delete TAG. Eagle fixture for tests/benchmarks: python3 tools/eagle-fixture.py OUT.library --items N [--seed S] [--unreadable] [--no-thumbnail-every K] and --mutate [--seed S] [--count N].

remote.distribution: `vamp-server serve --dist DIR` (env VAMP_DIST; default <VAMP_HOME>/dist when it exists) serves, WITHOUT any authentication (no token, no Tailscale allowlist check, in every --auth mode), GET|HEAD /install.sh (POSIX installer whose base URL is http://<request Host>) and /dist/<path> (plain-name segments only: [A-Za-z0-9._+-], no leading '.', otherwise 404). dist/build.sh [TARGET...] fills DIR from the repo: <target>/{vamp (feature remote), vamp-media, SHA256SUMS} for x86_64/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu (cargo-zigbuild, glibc 2.28) and aarch64/x86_64-apple-darwin, plus SKILL.md. `curl -fsSL http://<authority>:7777/install.sh | sh` picks the target from uname, verifies SHA256SUMS, installs into ${VAMP_INSTALL_DIR:-~/.local/bin} by rename, copies SKILL.md to ~/.claude/skills/vamp/ when ~/.claude exists, then runs `vamp join <base>` (VAMP_NO_JOIN=1 skips; a failed join prints the retry command and the install still succeeds). Re-running upgrades in place. clients/apple/release-mac.sh adds Vampire.dmg, mac/Vampire-<version>-<build>.dmg and appcast.xml.
remote.server: vamp-server (crates/vamp-server, tiny_http) serves one local authority library: `vamp-server token [--context X]` prints/creates <state_dir>/server-token (0600); `vamp-server serve [--context X] [--bind 127.0.0.1:7777] [--threads 16]`. Replica contexts cannot be served. serve also drains processor jobs (captions, tags, embeddings) on its own connection every --jobs-interval seconds (default 5) using run_jobs and the exclusive worker lock, so an external `vamp jobs watch` takes precedence; --no-jobs disables it. `vamp-server install-agent [--context X] [--bind B] [--no-jobs] [--dist DIR] [--force]` writes ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.vamp.server.<context>.plist (RunAtLoad, KeepAlive, VAMP_HOME/VAMP_MEDIA_HELPER/PATH captured, log ~/Library/Logs/vamp-server-<context>.log; --dist is passed to serve as an absolute path) without loading it and prints the launchctl bootstrap/bootout commands. `--bind tailnet[:PORT]` resolves this machine's Tailscale IPv4 (default port 7777) via the tailscale CLI ($VAMP_TAILSCALE, `tailscale` on PATH, or /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale).
remote.storage_isolation: Originals and Eagle library files may sit on cloud-synced folders (Google Drive File Provider) whose open/stat/read can block indefinitely. Catalog-only requests never touch them (browse/inspect report available_locally.original from the catalog: a cataloged local path counts as local). GET /v1/assets/{id}/{kind} runs on 16 dedicated media threads (HTTP workers only hand them over; 64 waiting -> immediate 503); the original's stat/open/hydration and every 256 KiB read run on a bounded request I/O pool (8 threads) with a 20 s inactivity deadline (first byte: 20 s from the request). On deadline the request answers 503 original_unavailable and the stuck call stays parked on the pool; a stall mid-body aborts the connection. On-demand thumbnail/preview generation runs on the same pool (callers wait up to 60 s; it attaches its result itself) and native hash hashes one original at a time there (a stall ends the batch). In vamp-core (jobs worker, Eagle thumbnail copy, uploads/evictions, lazy hashing, generate, CLI) original reads run on a shared background pool (32 threads, 60 s inactivity deadline extended by read progress); a stalled item is deferred, not failed: jobs go back to pending without spending an attempt (run_jobs reports deferred), uploads stay pending, Eagle thumbnails stay queued, and the batch moves on or stops. serve exits with status 70 (launchd KeepAlive restarts it) when every HTTP worker is busy and none finished a request or sent a body chunk for 60 s, or when every request I/O thread has been stuck on one call for 10 min, logging the busy requests and pool state first.
remote.auth: `vamp-server serve --auth token|tailscale`; default tailscale when bound to a tailnet address (100.64.0.0/10 or fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48), else token. A valid `Authorization: Bearer <token>` is accepted in every mode. With tailscale auth, a request from a tailnet address is resolved with `tailscale whois --json <ip>` (cached per IP 60 s, failures too) and admitted when the peer's user LoginName is in the allowlist (the pseudo-user `tagged-devices` never matches by user) or any of its node tags is. Allowlist: <state_dir>/tailnet-allow.json {users:[login], tags:[tag:x]}, re-read per request; absent = the server machine's own Tailscale user. `vamp-server allow [--user L]... [--tag tag:x]... [--remove]` edits it and prints it. Denials are 401 whose message names the peer and the exact `vamp-server allow --tag/--user` command. Otherwise 401. OPTIONS preflight needs no auth.
remote.cors: Origins chrome-extension://, moz-extension://, safari-web-extension:// are echoed in Access-Control-Allow-Origin (Vary: Origin); preflight 204 allows GET, POST, DELETE, OPTIONS and headers Authorization, Content-Type, Range. Other origins get no CORS headers.
remote.errors: JSON {error:{code,message}}; 400 bad_request, 401 unauthorized, 404 not_found, 409 conflict (revision), 413 too_large, 416 invalid range, 503 original_unavailable (original storage not responding; error.retry_after seconds, also a Retry-After header).

endpoints.GET /v1/hello: {library_id, name, protocol_version, auth: tailscale|token, peer: {login, tags, node}|null (null for bearer-token callers)}; used by `vamp join`.
endpoints.GET /v1/health: Never takes the library lock. {status: ok|degraded (an I/O pool is fully busy or holds an operation past its deadline), uptime_ms, http: {threads, busy, last_progress_ms_ago, oldest_request: {url, age_ms}|null}, io: {requests|background: {threads, busy, queued, saturation, oldest_op_ms, completed, stalled, running: [{label, age_ms}]}}, subsystems: {jobs|events: {last_beat_ms_ago}, library_lock: {held_ms|null}, media: {threads, busy}}}
endpoints.GET /v1/snapshot: Replica bootstrap, gzip when accepted: {library_id, cursor, assets: [AssetView] (live and trashed, current representations/observations), collections: [Collection with asset_ids], smart_folders: [SmartFolder], tags: {groups, starred}}, all read in one transaction; cursor = newest event sequence it reflects. GET /v1/hello also reports cursor.
endpoints.POST /v1/assets/batch: {ids (max 1000)} -> [AssetView] for ids that exist (absent = removed), gzip when accepted
endpoints.POST /v1/thumbnails/pack: {ids (max 512), kind: grid|micro} -> application/x-vamp-pack: per id in order, u16le id length, id, u32le data length, data (length 0 = none). grid = the 400 px JPEG, else the current thumbnail; micro = the catalog micro-thumbnail. Replica thumbnail downloads use 8 concurrent packs of 32.
endpoints.GET /v1/events/stream?after=N&wait=30&li: Long-poll push: answers [Event] (as /v1/events) as soon as an event with sequence > after exists, else [] after wait seconds (max 60). A server watcher polls the catalog's newest sequence every 100 ms, so writes by any process (CLI, app, importer) wake waiters; each stream request runs on its own thread.
endpoints.GET /v1/search?q=&limit=100&semantic=1&h: {semantic, results:[{asset, score}]} ranked by the authority embedder; without an embedder or query: FTS matches, score null, semantic:false
endpoints.GET /v1/embeddings/pack/meta: {version, model, dim, palette_dim, count, quant, bytes}; {count:0, version:null} without embeddings. Builds/refreshes the pack under the library lock (cached afterwards).
endpoints.GET /v1/embeddings/pack: application/octet-stream energy pack (see models.energy_pack), ETag = quoted version; 404 no_embeddings.
endpoints.GET /v1/assets/{id}: AssetView {asset, representations, observations}; 404 when absent or removed
endpoints.GET /v1/assets/{id}/{thumbnail|preview|o: bytes; ETag = quoted blake3 (original hash — the pending source key while the original's fingerprint is lazy — or of the derivative file); If-None-Match -> 304; single Range bytes=a-b|a-|-n -> 206 with Content-Range
endpoints.POST /v1/ingest?filename=&name=&source_u: raw body (<= 1 GiB) -> Asset; bytes stored via Library::ingest_bytes in the inbox; name renames after ingest; note maps to metadata.description
endpoints.POST /v1/clip: {url, title?, image_url?, tags?, note?, html?} -> Asset. With image_url: downloads (http(s), 30 s timeout, <= 64 MiB, 5 redirects) and ingests; filename from URL or Content-Type. Without: stores an Internet Shortcut `.url` file ([InternetShortcut] URL=...). name = title (else url for bookmarks); source_url = url; description = note; metadata.extra.clip = {page_title, image_url}. html is accepted and ignored.
endpoints.POST /v1/native: {operation, ...native request fields except home/context} -> the native result for the served library. Allowed: browse, galaxy, galaxy_search, sidebar, collections, inspect, tags, smart_folders, update, remove, restore, empty_trash, touch, collection_create, collection_move, smart_folder_create/update/delete, tag_rename, tag_delete, palette, hash; others 400.
endpoints.GET /v1/assets/{id}/original?redirect=1: 302 to a 15-minute presigned S3 GET URL when the original is S3-stored (optional; bearer token not forwarded). Otherwise identical to the stream endpoint, which rehydrates cloud-only originals on the authority before streaming.
endpoints.POST /v1/jobs/claim: {worker_id, processors:[name], limit=1 (1-100), lease_seconds=120 (1-3600)} -> {protocol_version, jobs:[{job: Job (status running, lease set), lease: {id, worker_id, expires_at}, input: original|thumbnail|preview, input_url: "/v1/assets/{asset_id}/{input}", request: ToolRequest (operation process, asset, library_id, event_id; input_path null — the worker sets it to its downloaded copy)}]}. Expired leases are reclaimed first. Only pending jobs of the named processors whose current registration has output observation and placement any|remote are leased.
endpoints.POST /v1/jobs/{id}/heartbeat: {lease_id, lease_seconds=120} -> {job} with the lease extended; 409 once the job is no longer held by that lease (reclaimed, completed, failed), 404 unknown job.
endpoints.POST /v1/jobs/{id}/complete: {lease_id, response: ToolResponse} -> {job} (completed). Applied through the local apply path in one transaction with the lease check: staleness (current original source key must equal job.source_hash) fails the job with 400 "stale result"; invalid responses fail it with 400; foreign/expired-and-reclaimed lease -> 409 and nothing is applied.
endpoints.POST /v1/jobs/{id}/fail: {lease_id, error} -> {job} (failed, error "worker <id>: <error>"); retry explicitly with vamp jobs retry. 409 when the lease is no longer held.

remote.derivatives: After ingest/clip of an image the server generates thumbnail+preview when the vamp-media helper is found (VAMP_MEDIA_HELPER, next to the executable, or ../Resources); failures leave the asset without derivatives.
remote.replica: A context with remote {url, token} whose state_dir holds an ordinary catalog mirror (library.json storage=replica) written only by sync; cursor in table replica_state. Mirror representation paths point into state_dir/cache/{thumbnail,preview}/; originals cache at state_dir/cache/original/<source key>.<ext> (verified against blake3 unless the authority fingerprint is still pending). browse/inspect/collections/tags/sidebar/smart_folders read the mirror and work offline. Native writes (update, remove, ingest, add, collection_create/rename/delete/add/remove) are forwarded to the server; restore, empty_trash, touch, collection_move, smart_folder_create/update/delete, tag_rename, tag_delete, palette, hash, batch update (asset_ids) and nested collection_create (parent_id) go through POST /v1/native; then sync runs. sync also mirrors smart folders and tag groups on smart_folder_updated / tag_groups_updated events. add uploads each file's bytes via /v1/ingest. Semantic browse on a replica is ranked by the authority (/v1/search?semantic=1) and rendered from the mirror; when the authority is unreachable or has no embedder it falls back to mirror FTS with semantic:false. similar forwards to /v1/assets/{id}/similar; accept_tags forwards then syncs. The CLI refuses mutating commands on replicas. import_eagle and export run only against a local authority. remote.token may be absent (tailscale identity auth). remote.drive_roots {authority_prefix: local_prefix} (optional). Originals on replicas are read directly, without download, when a local candidate exists with the cataloged byte_size and (when hashed) matching blake3 (verified once; <state_dir>/cache/direct/<blake3 prefix> remembers path/size/mtime): candidates are the authority path itself, the longest whole-component drive_roots prefix match, and for authority paths under */Library/CloudStorage/<provider>/ the same relative path under this user's ~/Library/CloudStorage/<provider>/ (e.g. GoogleDrive-<same account>). Otherwise the original downloads into cache/original.
remote.config: config.json (and every atomically written catalog JSON) is created 0600 because it may hold remote tokens. `vamp contexts list/use` redact tokens.
remote.cli: Feature `remote` of vamp-cli: `vamp contexts remote <name> --url URL --token T` (attach + initial sync), `vamp sync [--context X]`; `vamp media fetch` downloads lazily on replicas; `vamp media search --semantic` on a replica is ranked by the authority (/v1/search?semantic=1) with documents from the mirror, reporting semantic:false when the authority has no embedder. `vamp join <host|host:port|http(s)://url> [--name N] [--drive-root AUTHORITY=LOCAL]...`: tokenless attach (GET /v1/hello supplies the default name) + initial sync; host defaults to port 7777. `vamp sync --watch`: initial sync then loops on /v1/events/stream (25 s), printing one JSON line {applied, cursor, changed, at_ms} per change; errors print {error, at_ms} and retry after 5 s. `vamp [--context X] sync install-service` (replica contexts only) keeps `vamp --home H --context X sync --watch` running: Linux writes ~/.config/systemd/user/vamp-sync-<X>.service (Restart=always) and returns {unit, enable: "systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now vamp-sync-<X>.service", notes}; macOS writes ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.vamp.sync.<X>.plist (KeepAlive, log ~/Library/Logs/vamp-sync-<X>.log) and returns {agent, log, load}.
remote.worker: `vamp worker --server URL (--token T | VAMP_SERVER_TOKEN | --token-file F) [--processors NAME]... [--concurrency N=1] [--worker-id ID=<hostname>:<pid>] [--lease-seconds 120] [--poll-seconds 5] [--exit-when-idle]` (feature remote) offers this machine's installed model processors (vamp setup models --install here; matched to the authority's registrations by name, local argv/timeout used) to the authority. Each of N slots loops: claim 1 job, download input_url to <home>/tools/worker/<job>/ (blake3-verified for settled originals), heartbeat every lease/3 while the local command runs, POST complete (or fail); a lost lease discards the result. Setup specs marked "serve": true (all three model processors; Florence and SigLIP accept --serve --socket PATH --idle-seconds N) run as warm servers at <home>/tools/worker-servers/<name>.sock (stderr in <name>.log, idle exit after 15 min), started on first use and shared by all slots; other processors run one-shot. Claim errors back off up to 60 s; the scratch dir is wiped on start, and a killed worker's jobs return to pending when their lease expires (failed after 3 attempts). Logs JSON lines on stderr (job_completed with download_ms/process_ms). `vamp worker install-service --server URL (--token T | --token-file F) [--processors]... [--concurrency N]` writes ~/.config/systemd/user/vamp-worker.service (Restart=always, PATH captured; --token is stored in <home>/worker-token 0600) and prints `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now vamp-worker.service`; enable lingering for login-less operation.

errors.encoding: ErrorResponse JSON on stderr; success JSON on stdout. Help/version are human-readable.
errors.job_failure: jobs run returns nonzero if any attempted job fails; inspect jobs list for structured durable errors. jobs watch continues after job failures but stops on fatal engine/output errors.

agent_guide: `vamp guide` prints docs/agents/SKILL.md (compiled in, YAML front matter stripped) as plain text, not JSON: discovery (commands/schema), search incl. --semantic/--hybrid/similar, inspect/fetch/sheet/export, MetadataPatch updates with --expected-revision, collections/smart folders, ingest, safety rules (trash not delete, no empty-trash/bulk/tag-wide changes without confirmation, never write into *.library). The same file is the Claude skill installed by /install.sh.

apple_client.name: Vampire (bundle ids dev.vamp.vampire.mac / dev.vamp.vampire.ios); reads the .vamp preview-library UTI dev.vamp.preview-library
apple_client.engine: Links vamp-bridge statically; every request goes through vamp_request on a background actor. Always sends browse `sort` (default added_desc). Unknown-operation/field errors are shown as a non-blocking notice, not an alert.
apple_client.helpers: At launch, if VAMP_MEDIA_HELPER is unset, the app sets it to Contents/Resources/vamp-media so add/ingest generate thumbnails and previews.
apple_client.intake: Finder files/folders (folders expanded client-side to visible regular files) -> add (referenced in place). Browser image data, file promises, ⌘V image, screenshots (`/usr/sbin/screencapture -i`), clipboard clips -> ingest (bytes into the library Inbox). A bare web URL is downloaded if it serves image/*, else stored as a .webloc bookmark with metadata.source_url.
apple_client.duplicate_alert: Mac intake (drop, paste, Import…) first screens files and bytes with find_duplicates off the main thread. Without matches intake proceeds unchanged. Otherwise a Duplicate File Alert (N) sheet shows one duplicate at a time (existing asset: thumbnail, Existing badge, name, W × H / size, folders or Uncategorized; incoming: preview, Imported badge) with Use existing file (default) | Keep both and Apply all(N): Use existing skips the import, files the existing asset into the current folder scope (collection_add) and selects it; Keep both imports a new asset (ingest of the bytes when the path is already that asset's original). Closing the sheet skips the remaining duplicates; non-duplicates are always imported.
apple_client.internal_drag: Grid items are dragged as pasteboard type dev.vamp.asset-id (one asset id per item); dropping onto a sidebar folder calls collection_add, onto Trash calls remove. Sidebar folders drag as dev.vamp.folder-id: dropped on a folder row's top edge = collection_move before it (same parent), elsewhere on the row = nest as last child, on the Folders header = move to root.
apple_client.viewer: Shows the local preview immediately (sized to the asset's width/height), calls `touch` (Recently Used), then the original from `original` (local; reading a Drive placeholder hydrates it) or `representation kind=original` (replica). While the original loads a spinner + Cancel keeps the preview; keys 0-5 set rating (update metadata.rating), F fit, A 100%.
apple_client.eagle_ui: Dark Eagle-style layout. Sidebar: library picker; All/Uncategorized/Untagged/Recently Used/Random/All Tags/Trash with counts from `sidebar`; Smart Folders (smart_folders, editor -> smart_folder_create/update/delete); nested Folders from `collections` parent_id/sort_order with counts from `sidebar`.folders; bottom name filter. Toolbar: back/forward scope history, zoom, Waterfall/Justified/Grid layout (client-side from asset width/height; tiles fill-crop thumbnails whose aspect disagrees, items without a thumbnail show a type placeholder), sort (incl. random+seed), filter-bar toggle, search. Filter bar maps to browse: Color -> colors+color_tolerance, Tags -> tags_any (Any) or tags (All), Folder -> folder_ids+include_subfolders, Shape -> shape, Rating -> rating_min, Types -> exts, + -> date_from/date_to and size_min/size_max (bytes; entered in MB). Folder scope sends collection_id+include_subfolders; Recently Used sends recently_used; Trash sends trash (Restore -> restore, Empty Trash -> empty_trash). Inspector: palette swatches (click -> colors filter), name/notes/URL (update), tags (+autocomplete), folders (inspect.folder_ids; Add to Folder -> collection_add), rating stars, dimensions/size/type/dates/storage/hash_state, Export -> export. Multi-select batch: update{asset_ids, metadata:{rating|add_tags|remove_tags}}, collection_add, remove. All Tags view: tags (groups) with tag_rename (merge) / tag_delete. File menu: Import Eagle Library… / Sync from Eagle -> import_eagle_start then import_status polled every 250 ms (determinate overlay: phase, done/total, new/updated/trashed; status.error is shown as the failure); a re-run is the incremental sync; the last path is remembered per library.
apple_client.grid_performance: Browse results live in a separate BrowseFeed observable (items, isLoadingMore) read only by the grid and the paging spinner, so a page arriving does not re-render sidebar/toolbar/inspector. Custom NSCollectionViewLayout keeps item frames in a flat array with a 400 pt vertical bucket index (rect queries O(visible)) and lays out appended pages incrementally; browse pages of 500 append via insertItems, requested while two screens of content remain; thumbnails decode off-main (ImageIO thumbnail API, 2-6 concurrent, size-bucketed 256-1024 px), NSCache 384 MB/3000 entries with a synchronous probe for reused cells, queued decodes cancelled when cells scroll away, one-screen look-ahead prefetch at low priority. Debug builds (or UI_DRIVER=1 build.sh) replay VAMP_UI_SCRIPT for scripted screenshots and scroll timing.
apple_client.replicas: remote_attach from 'Connect to Server…' (modes: 'Tailnet host' = host[:port] with no token, default name from the host; 'URL + token') or, on iOS, 'Connect via Tailnet' (host default jmills-mac-mini, port 7777, optional token; empty token = Tailscale identity). While a replica is current the app loops sync_wait off the engine actor (reloading on applied > 0; 15 s backoff on error) and keeps the 60 s sync poll as fallback; also syncs on selection and after every write.
apple_client.packaging: clients/apple/release-mac.sh: Release build (VERSION, BUILD default UTC yyyymmddHHMM), embeds vamp-media, vamp (feature remote), vamp-server and vamp-store in Contents/Resources, signs inside-out with IDENTITY (default first 'Developer ID Application', else 'Apple Development'; hardened runtime, timestamp), notarizes+staples when NOTARY_PROFILE (Developer ID only), writes DIST_DIR (default <repo>/dist)/mac/Vampire-<version>-<build>.dmg, copies it to Vampire.dmg and regenerates appcast.xml with Sparkle generate_appcast (enclosures $DIST_URL/mac/, default DIST_URL http://jmills-mac-mini:7777/dist). build.sh uses xcodebuild when full Xcode is selected (MAC_BUILD_SETTINGS passes extra settings), else compiles the mac app with swiftc (Command Line Tools only; no updater; iOS needs Xcode). clients/apple/release-ios.sh archives VampIOS (Release, automatic signing) and with ASC_KEY_ID/ASC_ISSUER_ID/ASC_KEY_PATH exports with destination=upload to App Store Connect/TestFlight; without them it exports an App Store (else development) IPA to build/ios/export, lists the missing variables and exits 3.
apple_client.updates: Mac only: Sparkle 2 (SPM). Info.plist SUFeedURL=$(SPARKLE_FEED_URL), SUPublicEDKey=$(SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY) stamped by release-mac.sh from the login-keychain EdDSA key (Sparkle generate_keys); builds with an empty key have no updater. On launch the updater starts and checks once in the background; App menu 'Check for Updates…'. Feed override: env VAMP_UPDATE_FEED or user default VampUpdateFeedURL. ATS NSAllowsLocalNetworking permits the plain-HTTP tailnet feed. Logs 'Vampire update: found <version> (build <n>)' / 'up to date' via NSLog.
